cube-yolo.int8.onnx.runtime: onnxruntime-web — NOT SHIPPED; the web build serves the fp32 graph
cube-yolo.int8.onnx.quantisation_note: quantises ACTIVATIONS as well as weights, and that is what costs the reads: 4 of 20 golden fixtures come back with a different face, two of them frames the fp32 graph correctly refuses. Contrast cube-yolo.tflite, which takes the same size reduction weight-only and diverges on none. Do not ship this without re-exporting weight-only.

cube-yolo.mlpackage.precision: fp16 compute, fp32 tensor in, fp16 out

cube-yolo.tflite.runtime: LiteRT/TFLite (onnx2tf) — NOT SHIPPED YET; the Android LiteRT backend is device-gated work, so Android runs the WebView fp32 path
cube-yolo.tflite.precision: dynamic-range int8: int8 weights, fp32 activations, fp32 I/O
cube-yolo.tflite.layout: NHWC input; box coords in 640-space (the read is scale-invariant, so the consumer need not rescale)
cube-yolo.tflite.quantisation_note: full-integer int8 (int8 activations) was rejected — it collapses the detect head's class scores to ~0 (NO_FACE on all golden frames); weight-only int8 reads identical to fp32 (0/20). Verified by ml/golden_frames.py.
